「俺さ……昔の編集さんに連絡してみたんだよね、10年ぶりに」と、彼は静かに切り出した。

「発売日に、その人、本屋に連れてって、その場で見せたかったな」と、友利は遠くを見るような目をした。

"Oh... what happened all of a sudden? This. No matter how many times I draw, it just doesn't work," the girl said, her shoulders slumping—her artistic talent seemed to have suddenly diminished, as if the vigor of her lines had vanished overnight.  
"That's why I called you," Mariha said, looking at Tomori with a serious expression.  
"Could you draw the continuation of that manga for me?" she pleaded.  
"Huh? Why? You've been drawing it yourself until now, right? Why can't you suddenly do it anymore?" Tomori asked, confused.  
"I don't know either. Is it a slump?" Mariha sighed.  
"If you ask a professional, it'll cost a lot," Tomori smirked.  
"I'll treat you to the Napolitan here as a thank you," Mariha negotiated.  
After a wry smile, Tomori suddenly turned serious.  
"I contacted my old editor, you know, after ten years," he quietly began.  
"Really? That's great," Mariha's tone suddenly matured.  
"Yeah, we're going to meet up," Tomori scratched his head shyly.  
"It's a bit awkward since I ghosted them after my serialization was decided back then," he continued.  
"Huh, serialization? I didn't hear about that," Mariha leaned forward in surprise.  
"Heh... isn't it amazing?" Tomori puffed out his chest, hiding his embarrassment.  
"There was someone I wanted to show it to first, so I kept it a secret from everyone," he murmured.  
From the way he spoke, it was easy to guess who that "person he wanted to show" was without even asking.  
"I wanted to take that person to the bookstore on the release day and show it to them right there," Tomori said, his eyes distant.  
At those words, a scene floated up from the depths of memory—a decade ago, when the young Takie peered at the manuscript Tomori had offered on that afternoon.  
"Huh?" Takie tilted her head playfully and leaned in to look at Tomori's hands.  
"Here you go," Tomori offered the notebook a bit proudly.  
"Huh?" Takie's eyes widened.  
"What?! Wow...! Where? Where is it?" she exclaimed excitedly, flipping through the pages.  
"Oh, this, at the beginning, this this this," Tomori pointed.  
"Wow! Amazing!" Takie cheered.  
"Wow, that's incredible, Tomori!" she beamed as if it were her own achievement.  
Back then, when their existence was taken for granted—only Takie's laughter continued to resonate in Tomori's ears, undimmed by time. Perhaps the reason he chose to meet with the new editor was that he desperately wanted to rewrite the continuation of that day.  
He suddenly glanced out the window, gazing at the mountain ridge. That ridge, which had been stripped bare by reckless deforestation during his father's time, was slowly regaining its greenery—though ten years is too short a time to recover what was lost, it is never too late to start something anew, he reminded himself.
